date_note: Tuoi Tre News published the Kaspersky figures on 21 November; the page gives no earlier release day, report name or survey period.

evidence.quote: Deepfake attacks account for 21 percent of cyberattacks in Vietnam, nearly double the global average of 11 percent
The survey found that 63 percent of organizations in APAC had been affected by attacks exploiting employees' lack of security awareness
In Vietnam, the figure reached 75 percent, the highest among the markets surveyed.

exec: Kaspersky survey data relayed by Tuoi Tre puts deepfakes at 21 percent of cyberattacks in Vietnam, against a global average of 11 percent.
plain: A Kaspersky survey reported by Tuoi Tre says deepfakes make up 21 percent of cyberattacks in Vietnam, almost double the 11 percent global average.

key_findings: Deepfake attacks account for 21 percent of cyberattacks in Vietnam, against a global average of 11 percent, according to Kaspersky data.
63 percent of organizations in APAC, and 75 percent in Vietnam, had been affected by attacks exploiting employees' lack of security awareness.

sources.name: Tuoi Tre News (Ngoc Nguyen, Duc Thien)

summary: Tuoi Tre News reports Kaspersky data showing deepfake attacks account for 21 percent of cyberattacks in Vietnam, nearly double the global average of 11 percent. According to the Kaspersky survey, 63 percent of organizations in APAC, and 75 percent in Vietnam, had been affected by attacks exploiting employees' lack of security awareness.
title: Kaspersky: deepfakes are 21 percent of cyberattacks in Vietnam, nearly double the global average

validation.note: Only Tuoi Tre News read; it relays Kaspersky survey data without naming the report, sample or period. Kaspersky's own release was not found or read.
